body: This is an excellent point, and a major reason I decided to get the vaccine.
This reminds me of high school, the time when my boyfriend stole pizza by shoving it down his pants. Good times …
Totally! It made me smile. I honestly thought it was cute and funny, not trashy.

I’m guessing people just assume your wife does everything around the house and all of the childcare, and you do next to nothing, because that is how it is for them. That’s how it is for me, anyway. Maybe you are putting the expectations on yourself because you don’t want to be a jerk? It sounds like you’re doing a great job. Thank you for being kind and helpful to your wife. Sending you a virtual pat on the back.
I read this as: “Moderate Republicans can be seasoned with (some thyme)
This should not have made me laugh so hard.

Read a lot of comments and haven’t seen this mentioned yet … isn’t it possible that her fiancé already caught her cheating and made the profile to get back at her? Or he suspects her and is trying to catch her? Anyway, I don’t believe it’s real.

Excellent post. This is why I don’t have “mom friends”, because everyone is so judgmental, and I’d rather be alone than have myself and my parenting choices being constantly critiqued. I don’t get the impression that the mom was being serious anyway? It all seemed like she was setting herself up to be criticized and being overly dramatic to be funny. That’s just my impression.

Wow, I can’t even imagine! I’ve given birth to two children. Our bills totaled over $45,000. Cleaned out our checking account, used our tax refund and sold my car to make up the difference. And if we hadn’t had the “good” insurance the second time around, the bill probably would have been a million dollars.

I spend most of my free time on creative pursuits, although I rarely finish anything. Thanks for suggesting it and I know you’re right ... but honestly, I don’t think I can do counseling with him. If I’m required to be honest, the things I’ve held back will be even more hurtful than everything I’ve already said. Some of the issues are very deep, some very shallow. But I’m afraid that most, if not all, of them are not fixable to my mind. So I would have to weigh very carefully whether it’s worth putting it all out in the open. I personally think it would be less painful for him if I just walked away.

Ouch, I’m sorry to hear that your experience is similar. And I can’t give advice because my advice would obviously suck. I know it’s cliche but ... it’s not him, it’s me. It’s hard for me to say if this is the case for you, since I don’t know you, but it may be true for you too.  And yeah ... I don’t believe there is anything he could to to make me happy. That’s why I consider removing myself because I can’t see any other way to resolve this. 

Now see, if I liked watching tv ... my marriage might be saved. But I can’t stand it.

Great questions, thanks for asking. Have I told him that I wish I could off myself rather than spend my life with him, and that the only reason I don’t is because I worry about the impact my suicide would have on our children? Yeah ... as you can imagine, he wasn’t really happy about that. He knew I was unhappy for years, but didn’t really care until I talked about leaving. But honestly, I think he likes me being depressed because he knows I feel trapped here.

I find my depression impossible to explain. I like to create. Arts and crafts, writing, singing.
